subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw officially support a best-effort standalone linux/riscv64 Docker tag built through a separate pinned Node distribution path while leaving default multi-arch tags unchanged?
rationale: The implementation is technically demonstrated, but accepting another official architecture, an alternate runtime supply chain, and weaker per-release availability is a release-ownership and product-policy choice.

options.title: Sponsor standalone tag
options.body: Accept a non-blocking riscv64-suffixed image with pinned provenance, explicit limitations, and no changes to existing default manifests or attestations.

options.title: Require full parity
options.body: Defer official support until riscv64 can meet the same manifest, variant, attestation, and availability guarantees as amd64 and arm64.

options.title: Decline official image
options.body: Leave riscv64 images community-owned to avoid adding an official release and supply-chain commitment.

recommendation.title: Sponsor standalone tag
recommendation.body: Accept a non-blocking riscv64-suffixed image with pinned provenance, explicit limitations, and no changes to existing default manifests or attestations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release and attestation work makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the official-image boundary.
